# SPE Round 5 Plan: invoice extraction (Q, R, S)

Round 4 left one miss. R predicted 0.95 field accuracy and measured 0.88. The naive guess of 0.90 was closer than my prediction. Q was a hit at 0.93. The cause is F9: the OCR cleanup tool drops line items on two-column layouts. This round tests a fix for F9 and keeps R unchanged as a control.

## 1. Specify

### Raw record
- I will save your pasted text and "go again" word for word in `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r05.md`. That file is never edited.

### Proposals from round 4

| Proposal | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1. Keep OCR cleanup but skip it on two-column layouts | Adopted as a new config, S | S is R plus a layout gate. It changes one thing. R stays as it is, so the eval can tie any difference to the gate. |
| P2. Add 15 scanned invoices with handwriting | Rejected for round 5. Logged as default D-r05-1. | The AP lead has not written reference fields for these 15 invoices, and I cannot write them myself. Q at 0.93 is not at the ceiling. Adding invoices would also change the eval set in the same round as the S fix, so the round 4 numbers would no longer be a fair baseline. |
| P3. Drop config P | Adopted | P trailed Q on every round 4 metric. P's round 4 numbers stay in the log as the baseline. Dropping P cuts trial spend by about a quarter. |

### Requirements (round 5)

I assume the round 4 table ended at R30. I will use the next free ID when I write `spe/spec/spec.md`.

| R31 | Each of the 60 invoices carries a layout tag (one-column or two-column). The tag is saved before any trial runs. | r04 F9 | `layout_tags.json` exists and has 60 entries. The grader refuses to run without it. |
| R32 | Config S runs OCR cleanup only on invoices its layout detector marks one-column. | r04 F9, P1 | The trace check confirms no cleanup tool call on any invoice the detector marked two-column. |
| R33 | The S layout detector agrees with the saved layout tags. | r04 F9 | `layout_detector_recall` on two-column invoices. |
| R34 | Line items on two-column invoices are measured on their own. | r04 F9 | `line_item_recall_2col`: code match of line items against AP lead references. |
| R35 | R's broken Why ("OCR cleanup fixes scanned totals") is measured directly. | r04 "Which Why broke" | `total_exact_scanned`: exact match of the total on scanned invoices only. |

## 2. Predict

Configs:
- **Q** (control): Sonnet 5.5, schema-first prompt. No change.
- **R** (control): Q plus OCR cleanup tool. No change.
- **S**: R plus a layout gate that skips OCR cleanup on two-column invoices. This is the one change.

A hit is a measured value inside the band. Naive guess is 0.90 for field accuracy, as in round 4.

The gate removes the F9 loss, so S should return to Q's level. I add no gain for cleanup on scanned totals, because round 4 showed that claim was unproven. |
| Line-item recall, two-column invoices | `line_item_recall_2col` (code) | 0.92 ± 0.05 | 0.70 ± 0.10 | 0.92 ± 0.05 | New metric | F9 says cleanup drops two-column line items. S skips cleanup there, so it should match Q. R's band is wide because I have not measured the size of the drop. |
| Total exact match, scanned invoices | `total_exact_scanned` (code) | 0.85 ± 0.07 | 0.90 ± 0.07 | 0.90 ± 0.07 | New metric | This tests R's broken Why directly. If cleanup helps scanned totals, R and S beat Q here. Scanned invoices are mostly one-column, so S keeps cleanup on them. |

Stop rule check: predictions have not matched for 3 rounds in a row, because R missed in round 4. The loop continues.

## 3. Evaluate

### Harness steps and gates
1. Tag the 60 invoices by layout and save `spe/evals/data/layout_tags.json` (R31). Gate: 60 entries, and you spot-check 10 per D-r05-2.
2. Build the S layout gate as a code change to R's tool routing. Gate: unit test on 3 known two-column and 3 known one-column invoices.
3. Grader selftest. Gate: the oracle answers pass every check, and empty and wrong answers fail every check.
4. Control regrade. Gate: regrading the saved round 4 outputs gives Q 0.93 and R 0.88 field accuracy. Any other value halts the run as a grader bug.
5. Dry run on 3 cells: one two-column invoice each for Q, R, and S. Gate: schema valid, traces readable, and S makes no cleanup call on the two-column invoice.
6. Full run. Trials get the extraction schema. Code checks run first. No judge is needed this round, because every metric is checked by code.
7. Peek scan. Any trial that read graders, reference fields, layout tags, or predictions is voided and logged.
8. Split cells get extra trials. These are invoices where the 2 trials disagree on any field. The cap is 2 extra trials per cell.
9. Failure analysis on every miss, then a completeness critic checks that every requirement R31 to R37 has a measured result.

### Workflow arguments (`spe/evals/harness/r05-workflow.js`)
- `ROUND = 5` (one constant. Prompt text reads it, and no round number is typed by hand.)
- `configs: ["Q", "R", "S"]`
- `invoices: 60` (manifest hash checked against round 4)
- `trials_per_cell: 2`, `max_extra_trials_per_split_cell: 2`
- `spend_cap_usd: 40`. Trials that would cross the cap are skipped and logged.

### Cost estimate (not measured)
- 60 invoices × 3 configs × 2 trials = 360 trials, plus up to about 60 extra trials on split cells.
- About 15k input and 2k output tokens per trial, which is about 7M tokens in total. I will compare this against the round 4 actual spend before launch. The run stays under the $40 cap.

I will halt and report if the spend cap is reached, if the control regrade fails, if a trial reads the answer key, or if a decision only you can make comes up.
